items.risk: Customer contract terminations demonstrate that contracted demand can erode before revenue realization.
Backlog realization depends on customer commitments, policy/permitting and delivery economics rather than backlog volume alone.
Contract termination evidence means backlog cannot be treated as equivalent to realized revenue.
Policy, permitting, financing and customer project economics can reduce backlog conversion independently of manufacturing execution.
Backlog volume can overstate resilience if termination rights or economic adjustments are material.

contradictions.contradiction: Backlog remains large and guidance was reaffirmed even as current-quarter revenue fell due partly to contract terminations.
Large backlog and reaffirmed guidance coexist with revenue pressure from customer terminations; this narrows confidence in backlog quality without invalidating current execution.
Current profitability and guidance support execution while terminations demonstrate non-zero demand fragility; both facts should remain represented.
